candidate.answerReason: The opposite-side condition makes the two parts of the required angle supplementary to 130° and 110°. They are 50° and 70°, giving 120°.

methods.label: Draw a parallel through E
methods.explanation: Through point \(E\), draw \(EF\parallel AB\). Then \(EF\parallel CD\), \(\angle B+\angle BEF=180^\circ\), and \(\angle D+\angle DEF=180^\circ\). Adding the two equations gives \(\angle B+\angle D+\angle BED=360^\circ\), so \(\angle BED=360^\circ-130^\circ-110^\circ=120^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses grade-7 auxiliary parallel construction, supplementary interior angles and angle arithmetic.

methods.label: Use triangle BDE
methods.explanation:
Use \(BD\) as a transversal to find the sum of the two angles of triangle \(BDE\) at \(B\) and \(D\). Let \(\alpha=\angle ABD\) and \(\beta=\angle CDB\). Since \(AB\parallel CD\), these same-side interior angles satisfy \(\alpha+\beta=180^\circ\). Because \(E\) lies between the parallels on the opposite side of \(BD\) from \(A\) and \(C\), ray \(BD\) splits \(\angle ABE\), and ray \(DB\) splits \(\angle CDE\). Hence
\[
\angle EBD+\angle BDE=(130^\circ-\alpha)+(110^\circ-\beta)=60^\circ.
\]
The triangle angle sum gives \(\angle BED=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses grade-7 parallel-line properties with the primary-school triangle angle sum.
